cases.why: F0: the first pair is created, (A, B), by the change that also makes it the global pair: A, a primary with no peer before, is withdrawn at once and B answers
F0: only the state false: a swap of the two roles inside one pair changes no node's peer, so there is no F0 and no event
F1: dead(A) and ready(B) hold for exactly 5 s: A's last Heartbeat at 20 s is 15 s old at 35 s, B reports A down, so F1 withdraws A at 40 s
F1: only the state false, A already withdrawn: dead(A) and ready(B) hold and nothing happens
F1: only dead(A) false, A keeps its Heartbeats and rounds and B reports it up: no action
F1: only ready(B) false, B's rounds fail so its probe state is down: A is dead and nothing moves
F1: the inputs break one tick before the timer (B's Heartbeat at 38.5 s says A is up): no action at 40 s, the timer starts again when B reports A down at 42.5 s and F1 comes 5 s after that tick
input hb: a Heartbeat arrives 0.5 s before the tick at which the last one would have passed 15 s, so the Heartbeat is still counted at 35 s and passes at 50 s, and F1 follows at 55 s
input probe: three passing rounds in a row make B up at the third round (15 s), the same tick on which hb(A) passes, so F1 comes at 20 s
input probe: the third round fails after two passes, so B is not up (a lone failure changes nothing and two passes are not three): three more passes make it up at 30 s and F1 comes at 35 s
input probe: three failing rounds in a row (25, 30, 35 s) make A down at 35 s, with its Heartbeats still arriving and B reporting it down, so dead(A) holds from 35 s and F1 comes at 40 s
input probe: two failing rounds and then a pass do not make A down: dead(A) never holds and nothing moves
input probe: a probe state that was never learned is unknown, not down: A has no round at all, its Heartbeats arrive and B reports it down, and nothing moves
input probe: B's last round is at 25 s, so B is unknown from 40 s, the tick on which the 5 s would end: no F1, and B never becomes ready again
input probe: B's last round is at 26 s, so B is still up at 40 s (14 s since its last round) and F1 comes at 40 s
input view: B's last Heartbeat is 10 s old at 40 s, so view(A) is none and the timer breaks on the tick it would have ended: no F1
input view: B's last Heartbeat is 9 s old at 40 s, so view(A) is still down and F1 comes at 40 s
flap rule: a withdrawal 3599 s after the failback is a flap: flap_until is a day ahead, the flapping alert follows, S is 1800 s
flap rule: a withdrawal 3600 s after the failback is no flap: S stays 300 s
F2: rd(A) and ready(B) hold for exactly 30 s: A lists one resolve path and it is unhealthy from 20 s, B has a healthy one, so F2 withdraws A at 50 s
F2: only the state false, A already withdrawn: no action
F2: only rd(A) false, its path is healthy: no action
F2: only ready(B) false, B's rounds fail: no action
F2: the inputs break one tick before the timer (a healthy Heartbeat of A at 48.5 s) and begin again with A's Heartbeat at 50 s, so F2 comes 30 s later, at 80 s

F2: only rd(A) false, A lists no resolve path at all (its Heartbeat has an empty upstreams list, as before the first health check) while B has a healthy one: rd needs at least one listed path and none healthy, so no action
flap rule in F2: A failed back 3599 s before the withdrawal at 50 s, so F2 sets flap_until a day ahead and raises the flapping alert after its own
input rd: B's last Heartbeat is 15 s old at 50 s, so B no longer reports a healthy path and ready(B) fails: no F2
input rd: B's last Heartbeat is 14.5 s old at 50 s: rd(A) and ready(B) still hold and F2 comes at 50 s
F3: A is withdrawn, fit(A) and view(A) up hold from 15 s (its third passing round), so after S = 300 s, at 315 s, A is cleared and its last_failback_at is set
F3: while now < flap_until S is 1800 s, so A comes back at 1815 s and not at 315 s, and the refreshes of F7 come meanwhile
F3: only fit(A) false, A reports isolated in every Heartbeat: no failback
F3: only view(A) up false, B's PeerView has A as not known: no failback
F3: only the state false, A is withdrawn and held: no failback (a Release must come first)
F3: only the state false, A is not withdrawn: nothing to do
F3: the inputs break one tick before the timer (A reports isolated at 313.5 s), so the 300 s begin again at 315 s and A comes back at 615 s, after the refresh at 600 s
F4: a Hold for A with B fit and not withdrawn is done at once: A is withdrawn and held, the flap rule does not run
F4: only fit(B) false (B is isolated): refused with the reason peer_not_fit
F4: only B withdrawn false (B is withdrawn, fit): refused with the reason peer_withdrawn
F4: C is in no pair, so every condition that presupposes a peer is false: refused with the reason not_paired, the first
F4: B is not fit and withdrawn: refused with the reason of the first condition that fails, peer_not_fit
F5: a Release for a held A is done: the hold is cleared and A stays withdrawn (F3 decides its return)
F5: only held false (A is not held): refused with the reason not_held
F5: a Release for a held node in no pair is done, and the node stays withdrawn
F6: a Force failback for a withdrawn A that is fit clears the withdrawal at once, sets last_failback_at, and no S is left
F6: a Force failback also clears a hold
F6: only withdrawn false (A is not withdrawn): refused with the reason not_withdrawn
F6: only fit(A) false (A is isolated): refused with the reason not_fit
F6: C is in no pair: refused with the reason not_paired, the first
F6: the first reason that fails, not_withdrawn, when A is neither withdrawn nor fit
input fit: a HeadNotice sent exactly 30 s ago is not yet required (more than 30 s), so a lagging A is fit and the Force failback is done
input fit: a HeadNotice sent 31 s ago is required, so A with applied_seq 4 below it is not fit: refused with not_fit
input fit: A has applied the entry of the HeadNotice (applied_seq 5) in time: fit, the Force failback is done
F7: ten minutes after the last signing event, with no flag change, a refresh is signed
F7: no refresh one tick before the ten minutes
F7: a refresh repeats every ten minutes, and it carries the stable period of a withdrawn node
F7: an event on the tick on which the refresh is due replaces it (a Release signs its own version), and the next refresh is ten minutes after that event
order: F1 and F2 are due for A on the same tick (50 s): F1 acts, A is withdrawn, F2 does not apply and the alert is the Withdrawal
order: F0 and F1 on one tick: C and D are made a pair at 40 s, the tick on which F1 is due for A, so F0 acts first and withdraws C, then F1 withdraws A
order: F1 for A and F3 for B due on the same tick (315 s): F1 acts first, withdraws A and clears B's withdrawal, so F3 for B has nothing to do
order: a Release for B read on the tick on which F1 acts for A: F1 clears B's withdrawal and hold, so the Release is refused with not_held
order: three Release requests read on one tick are decided in requested_at order, then id: d (requested at 4 s), then c1 and c2 (both at 5 s)
order: a request read 10 s after its requested_at is decided (a request is expired only when older than 10 s)
order: a request read 10 s plus one tick after its requested_at is expired and never carried out

worst case of 8a.3: A dies just after a passing round and its last Heartbeat (at the kill). Its probe is down at 17 s, its Heartbeat is 15 s old at 16 s, B's down view reaches the hub at 22.5 s, and F1 acts 5 s after the next tick, 27.5 s after the kill (about 28 s)

worst case of 8a.3 with the last Heartbeat of A 4.9 s before the death: the hub's own Heartbeat signal comes earlier, at 111 s, but the decision still waits for B's down view, so F1 is at the same 27.5 s
outage: A's dns is down for 5 s from 50 s, 0 s into the 5 s round grid: at most 2 rounds in a row fail, which is below the 3 that make A down, so nothing moves
outage: A's dns is down for 5 s from 51 s, 1 s into the 5 s round grid: at most 2 rounds in a row fail, which is below the 3 that make A down, so nothing moves

outage: A's dns is down for 5 s from 54 s, 4 s into the 5 s round grid: at most 2 rounds in a row fail, which is below the 3 that make A down, so nothing moves
outage: A's dns is down for 6 s from 50 s, 0 s into the 5 s round grid: at most 2 rounds in a row fail, which is below the 3 that make A down, so nothing moves
outage: A's dns is down for 6 s from 51 s, 1 s into the 5 s round grid: at most 2 rounds in a row fail, which is below the 3 that make A down, so nothing moves
outage: A's dns is down for 6 s from 52 s, 2 s into the 5 s round grid: at most 2 rounds in a row fail, which is below the 3 that make A down, so nothing moves
outage: A's dns is down for 6 s from 53 s, 3 s into the 5 s round grid: at most 2 rounds in a row fail, which is below the 3 that make A down, so nothing moves
outage: A's dns is down for 6 s from 54 s, 4 s into the 5 s round grid: at most 2 rounds in a row fail, which is below the 3 that make A down, so nothing moves

outage: A's dns is down for 25 s from 50 s with its agent alive: five rounds fail, A is down at 62 s, B's own three failed rounds (shifted 2.5 s) end at 64.5 s and ride its Heartbeat at 67.5 s, so dead(A) holds from 68 s and F1 acts at 73 s

outage: A's dns is down for 30 s from 50 s with its agent alive: five rounds fail, A is down at 62 s, B's own three failed rounds (shifted 2.5 s) end at 64.5 s and ride its Heartbeat at 67.5 s, so dead(A) holds from 68 s and F1 acts at 73 s
a dead agent beside a live dns: A's Heartbeats stop at 20 s but its probes pass and B sees it up, so hb(A) is false from 35 s and nothing moves
a dead dns beside a live agent: A's Heartbeats go on, its rounds fail from 25 s (down at 35 s) and B reports it down from its Heartbeat at 37.5 s, so F1 acts at 43 s
a full cut of the panel's path to A while B marks A up: no Heartbeat, every round fails, and view(A) is up, so the hub's two signals never decide alone and nothing moves in 100 s
a frozen hub prober while A's dns dies: the last rounds are at 40 s, A's dns dies at 45 s and B reports it down, but every probe state is unknown from 55 s, so there is no F1
the advertised fallback B dies while the recovered primary A is inside S: F1 for B needs only ready(A), so it withdraws B and clears A's withdrawal at once, and the answer moves back to A
the advertised fallback B dies while the recovered primary A is flapping: F1 for B needs only ready(A), so it withdraws B and clears A's withdrawal at once, and the answer moves back to A

the advertised fallback B dies while the recovered primary A is held: F1 for B needs only ready(A), so it withdraws B and clears A's withdrawal and hold (the cleared-hold alert) at once, and the answer moves back to A
both nodes down, the withdrawn primary A returns first: B's death is seen by both observers (A's view and B's missing Heartbeats) once A is up at 115 s, so F1 for B clears A's withdrawal at 120 s
both nodes down, the advertised fallback B returns first while A is withdrawn: nothing moves, the answer is on B
both nodes down, neither withdrawn, the fallback B returns first: A has been silent and B sees it down, so F1 for A withdraws it at 120 s
both nodes down and silent: no view, so dead(X) holds for neither and nothing moves

hub restart with a withdrawn node: the start event is the F7 refresh, every probe state is unknown again, so nothing moves until three rounds after the restart (75 s) and F3 comes S after that, at 375 s, not at 315 s

hub restart with a held node: B dies at 40 s and F1 for B would be at 58 s, but the hub restarts at 50 s, so hb(B) counts from 50 s and A's probe is unknown until 65 s: F1 for B comes at 70 s and clears A's withdrawal and hold
a Hold at 20 s, a Release at 2020 s (2000 s later) and F3 only S = 300 s after the Release, at 2320 s; the refresh comes every 600 s meanwhile

B keeps marking the recovered primary A down: view(A) is never up, so F3 never comes in 400 s. A Force failback at 400 s moves it, and when A dies at 420 s F1 withdraws it again 20 s later with the flap rule (less than 3600 s after the failback): flapping alert, S 1800 s

A is withdrawn and F3 brings it back at 315 s; from 400 s its only resolve path is unhealthy while B's is healthy, so F2 withdraws it at 430 s, 115 s after the failback: flap_until is a day ahead and the flapping alert follows the F2 alert
upstream mode: both of A's upstreams are unhealthy from 20 s, so rd(A) holds and F2 acts at 50 s
upstream mode: one of A's two upstreams is healthy, so it still resolves and nothing moves
recursive mode, through the entry of the local Unbound: F2 acts at 50 s. While rd lasts there is no F3 (A is not ready), and it comes only S after the path is back at 100 s, at 400 s, not at 350 s
a cut of every resolve path on both nodes: rd is comparative and holds for neither, so nothing moves

B is withdrawn by F2 at 53 s (its first unhealthy Heartbeat is at 22.5 s), then A dies at 60 s with a last Heartbeat that lists a healthy path: rd(B) still holds while that Heartbeat is fresh, so B is not ready, and F1 for A comes only when it is 15 s old, at 75 s, plus 5 s: it withdraws A and clears B
A is revoked at 30 s while B is ready: revoked(A) is the one fact the hub acts on, dead(A) holds at once, and F1 acts 5 s after the revocation is read
A is revoked while its peer B is held: F1 withdraws A and clears B's withdrawal and hold, with the cleared-hold alert
A is revoked while B is not ready (its rounds fail): F1 needs ready(B), so nothing moves
after A was revoked and withdrawn, B dies at 70 s: F1 for B needs ready(A), and a revoked node is never ready, so the answer stays on B's address and nothing clears A
B keeps marking the recovered primary A down and is revoked at 30 s: F1 for B needs ready(A), which holds, so it withdraws B and clears A's withdrawal: the answer moves to A
a first pair (A, B) made while both nodes run: A is withdrawn by F0 at 10 s, B answers, and A is back by F3 300 s after fit(A) holds from 15 s, at 315 s

pairs (A, B) and (B, A) created together from no pair: step 1 withdraws A and B, step 2 decides both pairs from that state and clears both fallbacks, which are both nodes, so neither ends withdrawn and each answers the pair it is the primary of

(B, C) with B dead and withdrawn changed to (A, B) and (B, A) with A new: step 1 withdraws A, step 2 clears A and B, step 3 withdraws C as it leaves; B answers (B, A) until F1 moves it to A once B is dead to both observers and A is ready, at 20 s, with no flapping alert

(A, C) with A dead and withdrawn changed to (A, B), B never withdrawn and in no pair: no flag changes, B answers at once and never A, and C leaves while its old peer A is withdrawn, so C is not withdrawn
a dead, withdrawn primary replaced, (A, B) to (C, B) with C running: C is withdrawn, B is kept, A keeps its withdrawal, and C is back by F3 300 s after fit(C) holds, at 315 s

the advertised fallback replaced while the primary is dead, (A, B) to (A, C) with A withdrawn: A is kept withdrawn, C answers at once, B is not withdrawn because A is, so a node still on the older entry answers B
a planned primary change (A, B) to (C, B) with A advertised: C is withdrawn, A is withdrawn as it leaves, B answers, and C is back by F3 at 315 s
the same change with B dead: B answers, then F1 moves the answer to C once C is ready (20 s), with no flapping alert, and F0 wrote no last_failback_at so S(B) is still 300 s
the membership change of (A, B) to (C, B) read only at a hub start: the start event is F0 and sets the same flags as the tick case
a withdrawn node with 250 s of its 300 s met that F0 gives a new peer while it stays withdrawn: F3 comes 300 s after the F0 event (565 s), not 50 s
the fallback replaced while the primary is advertised, (A, B) to (A, C): no move, the old fallback B is withdrawn as it leaves
a pair replaced by two new nodes, (A, B) to (C, D): C is withdrawn, D answers at once, A and B keep their flags (a node that leaves every pair while its old peer leaves too is not evaluated)
a held primary whose fallback is replaced, (A, B) to (A, C): the hold is kept, the new fallback answers, and there is no cleared-hold alert
a new primary beside a held fallback, (A, B) with B held to (C, B): C is withdrawn, B's withdrawal and hold are cleared with the alert and B answers, A is withdrawn as it leaves

a dead, withdrawn primary whose advertised fallback is replaced by a held node, (A, B) to (A, C): C's hold is cleared with the alert and C answers, A stays withdrawn and is never answered, B is not withdrawn because A is
a new primary beside a revoked, withdrawn fallback, (A, R) to (C, R): step 1 withdraws C, step 2 clears C because R is revoked, so C answers and R never does
(N, R) with R revoked while in no pair and N just enrolled: step 1 withdraws N and R, step 2 clears N, so N answers and R never does
two held nodes put into one pair, (A, B): the fallback's hold is cleared, with the alert

a switch of the global pair from (A, B) to an existing (C, D): no node's peer changes, so there is no F0 and no event, and every flag is kept (A then drains on the node, which is not an output of the evaluator)

(A, B) with B dead and withdrawn; B replaced by C with no move (B keeps its withdrawal); A dies and F1 withdraws it at 43 s; then (A, B) is restored with B repaired: A stays withdrawn, B is cleared and answers at once, C is left not withdrawn because A is withdrawn, and A is back by F3 300 s after fit(A) and view(A) up first hold, at 383 s

the same sequence with B still down: the flags after the restore are the same, nothing moves while A is down too, and F1 for B moves the answer to A at 85 s, 5 s after A is ready (80 s) and B is dead to both observers (75 s), with no flapping alert for B
